brave.snippet:
Mcdonald's (MCD), ranking 44th by market capitalization reported its fiscal 2025 Q1 earnings on May 12th, 2025. McDonald's reported a decline in both revenue and net income, missing analyst expectations. The company's net income decreased by 3% from the previous year, reflecting a challenging economic environment.
Revenue McDonald's experienced a 4.7% decrease in total revenue for Q1 2025, amounting to $5.79 billion compared to $6.08 billion in Q1 2024. Revenue from franchised restaurants was $3.66 billion, while sales from company-owned and operated restaurants reached $2.13 billion. Additionally, other revenue streams contributed $162 million, bringing total revenues to $5.96 billion. Earnings/Net Income McDonald's EPS fell by 2.2% to $2.61 in Q1 2025, down from $2.67 in Q1 2024.
Kempczinski emphasized the importance of adapting to current market challenges, particularly in light of consumer uncertainty, stating that McDonald's is well-positioned to leverage its strong brand to attract customers. Guidance Management maintained its full-year outlook for net restaurant growth to contribute slightly over 2% to systemwide sales growth, with operating margins expected to be in the mid- to high-40% range. Analysts expect a revenue of approximately $6.1 billion for Q2 2025, with an estimated earnings per share of $3.12 for the fiscal quarter ending June 30, 2025.

brave.snippet:
Mcdonald's (MCD), ranking 41st by market capitalization reported its fiscal 2025 Q1 earnings on Apr 30th, 2025. McDonald's first-quarter results fell short of expectations as market challenges weighed heavily on performance. Revenue declined by 3% to $5.95 billion, missing analysts' forecast of $6.09 billion, while net income dropped 3% to $1.86 billion.
Revenue McDonald's reported a 4.7% revenue decrease, totaling $5.79 billion for Q1 2025, compared to $6.08 billion in Q1 2024. Franchised restaurants contributed $3.66 billion, while company-owned outlets generated $2.13 billion. Other revenue sources added $162 million, culminating in total revenues of $5.96 billion. Earnings/Net Income McDonald's experienced a decrease in EPS, dropping 2.4% to $2.61 in Q1 2025 from $2.68 in Q1 2024, alongside a 3.2% decline in net income to $1.87 billion.
Post Earnings Price Action Review The earnings report metrics had a moderate impact on McDonald's stock price, as a backtest from April 30, 2020, to April 30, 2025, indicated. Revenue showed a 3-Day win rate of 53.67%, while both the 10-Day and 30-Day win rates stood at 56.06% and 56.30%, respectively, suggesting short-term gains are somewhat likely post-earnings. Net income and EPS mirrored this pattern, with the 10-Day and 30-Day win rates also at 56.06% and 56.30%. The maximum observed return was 3.63% over 30 days.
Overall, all three metrics—revenue, net income, and EPS—suggest potential for modest positive gains following earnings releases, indicating opportunities for investors. brave.title: McDonald's (MCD) Q1 2025 earnings
brave.snippet:
The fast-food giant reported first-quarter net income of $1.87 billion, or $2.60 per share, down from $1.93 billion, or $2.66 per share, a year earlier. Excluding restructuring charges and other items, McDonald's earned $2.67 per share.
That drop is the worst in McDonald's home market since the 8.7% plunge during the second quarter of 2020, when states imposed lockdowns to slow the spread of Covid. Analysts surveyed by StreetAccount were expecting the company to report domestic same-store sales declines of 1.7% for the first quarter. "In the U.S., overall [quick-service restaurant] industry traffic from the low-income consumer cohort was down nearly double digits versus the prior year quarter," CEO Chris Kempczinski said on the company's conference call.
And even though high-income consumers are still dining out, their spending is not enough to offset the shrinking traffic from other income cohorts. Across all of its markets, McDonald's same-store sales fell 1% during the quarter, hurt by comparisons to last year's leap day, the company said.
McDonald's also plans to keep its $5 meal deal for the rest of 2025.

context.title: Darden vs. McDonald’s: Which Restaurant Stock Is the Better Buy for Income Investors
context.snippet:
Two restaurant stocks pay nearly identical dividends, but one cut its payout to the bone during the last downturn while the other kept raising through every storm. For retirees, that difference changes everything about which one belongs in a portfolio.
Story Continues Business Model Durability: Franchising Gives McDonald's the Edge Darden owns and runs its 2,218 restaurants, including Olive Garden, LongHorn Steakhouse and Yard House. That means it covers food, labor and occupancy costs directly. Its restaurant-level EBITDA margin last quarter was 18.8%. McDonald's is mostly franchised, with about 46,028 restaurants and a large real estate business underneath, so it takes in rent and royalties. The result is a 46.1% operating margin and fiscal 2025 free cash flow of $7.19 billion. Darden is performing better right now. Combined same-restaurant sales rose 3.1% in fiscal Q1, every segment grew, and LongHorn posted its 22nd consecutive quarter of positive same-restaurant sales. On the call, the chief executive said "Consumers are still spending. They're still resilient." McDonald's global comps slowed to 1.3% in Q2, and July U.S. comps were "slightly negative." Net sales dropped 3% to $5.96 billion.
